headline: The Asian liquidation finally came home: SPX -1.9%, VIX +18.7% to 22.91 with the term structure flat at 0.995, and the engine is a 2.91% real 10-year sitting alongside 6th-percentile breakevens.
summary: What changed overnight is location. For three sessions the damage was offshore; today the US paid. SPX -1.9% to 7,416.6, NDX -2.7%, and for the first time in this drawdown the front end of vol is bid in size: VIX +18.7% to 22.91 (it was 20.81 yesterday), VIX3M 23.02, and VIX/VIX3M at 0.995 after +6.3% — effectively flat, no longer a complacent 0.936. Note what is NOT driving it: SKEW -13.2% on the month at z=-2.0 with acceleration -2.63. Nobody is paying up for tails; they are selling spot delta. Asia got worse, not better — Taiwan -6.9% today after -6.0% yesterday (z=-2.59, acc -1.93), KOSPI -4.7% and 23.4% below its 200-day, Nikkei -3.4% and -9.6% on the month. The US-listed proxies still have not marked it: EWT last printed -12.2% on the month, EWY -10.7%.

The mechanism is a real-rate shock dressed as disinflation. 10-year 5.15% (+5bp), 10-year TIPS real yield 2.91% (+5bp, +50bp in three months, 29.5% above its 200-day), 2-year 4.88% after +37bp in a week, 30-year 5.47%. Simultaneously 10-year breakevens fell to 2.20% (-4bp, -15bp on the month, 6th percentile of the year) and 5-year to 2.25%. Crude cracked — WTI -3.9% to 85.09 and -16.1% on the month (z=-1.64), Brent -4.3%, gasoline -5.0% and -23.0% on the month. Falling inflation compensation plus rising real yields is the market telling you policy stays tight into a softening nominal economy, and bond vol agrees: MOVE 101.28, +17.8% in a week, +33.9% in three months. That combination is poison for long-duration cash flows and the factor tape shows it — growth/value z=-2.48, MTUM z=-2.02, high-beta/low-vol -13.6% on the month, semis/S&P z=-2.02, NVDA -26.4% on the month and pinned at the 0th percentile of its year.

What still refuses to break is credit and breadth, and that is the whole argument against de-risking wholesale. HY OAS 3.23, up just 3bp on a -1.9% equity day and -2bp on the month; IG 0.89; CCC +2bp; BKLN at the 97th percentile; HYG/IEF +1.6% on the week. Equal-weight S&P was +0.2% while the index fell 1.9%; RSP/SPY z=3.11 with acceleration 2.83, SPW at the 95th percentile, Dow Transports +0.3%. The macro underwriting it is intact: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), capacity utilisation at the 100th percentile, growth pulse +3. The quiet warnings are IG and BBB spread z-scores of 0.78 and 0.89 (widening steadily even as HY sits still), bank reserves -2.3% on the month, and NFCI tightening at z=0.31.

FX remains the most violent part of the tape and it is still a dispersion trade, not a blanket EM unwind. USDBRL 5.7838, +2.1% today, +13.5% on the month, z=3.81 with acceleration 2.80 — the single most extreme reading on the board and re-accelerating for a second day; Bovespa z=-3.39, EWZ -24.4% on the month. DXY 103.62 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.1002 at the 0th, USDCHF and USDCAD both at the 100th, AUDUSD -0.6% (z=-0.98) and AUD/JPY -0.8% and rolling over. Against that, India's Sensex is z=2.89 with acceleration 2.59 and INDA +9.4% on the month, Mexico's IPC +6.6%, the DAX +5.7% on the month at the 99th percentile, CAC +6.3%. Leadership at home is cash-flow-now and defensive: XLP at the 100th percentile, XLV +8.6% on the month with +10.8% relative strength, LLY +19.6%, HD +18.0% (z=2.43), UPS +17.4%, COST +12.8%, SPLV z=1.95. Own that side, fund it in semis, high beta and crypto — BTC 64,582 (-21.3% 1m), SOL -31.1%, COIN at the 0th percentile.

good.text: Credit still will not confirm the equity tape: HY OAS only +3bp to 3.23 on a -1.9% S&P day and -2bp over the month, IG 0.89, BKLN at the 97th percentile of its year, HYG/IEF +1.6% on the week.
Breadth is the opposite of a crash: equal-weight S&P +0.2% while the cap-weighted index fell 1.9%, RSP/SPY at z=3.11 with acceleration 2.83, SPW at the 95th percentile, Transports +0.3%.

The gasoline collapse is a consumer tax cut: RBOB -23.0% on the month (z=-2.10), WTI -16.1%, and retail is already capturing it — XRT +7.5% on the month with +9.7% relative strength, WMT +10.3%, COST +12.8%, HD +18.0% at z=2.43.
Mortgage rates are easing against the Treasury move — 30-year at 7.11%, -29bp on the month with acceleration -2.36 — and housing equities have run with it: ITB +12.7% 1m, XHB +9.9%, XHB/SPY z=2.22.

The labour and output data are still solid: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), industrial production +0.63 and capacity utilisation at the 100th percentile. Growth pulse +3.

Defensive-but-rising leadership keeps compounding rather than hiding in cash: XLV +8.6% 1m (98th pctile, +10.8% RS), XLP at the 100th percentile, SPLV z=1.95, USMV at the 97th, LLY +19.6% on the month.
Europe and India are decoupling from the Asia-tech unwind: DAX +5.7% on the month at the 99th percentile, CAC +6.3%, Sensex z=2.89 with acceleration 2.59, INDA +9.4% 1m and +11.6% relative strength.

bad.text: Real yields are doing the damage: 10-year TIPS 2.91% (+5bp today, +50bp in three months, 29.5% above its 200-day) while 10-year breakevens fell to 2.20%, the 6th percentile of the year. Tight policy into falling inflation compensation.

The front end is being repriced hawkishly and fast — 2-year 4.88% after +37bp in a week, 2s10s back to 29bp at the 17th percentile — and bond vol broke 100: MOVE 101.28, +17.8% on the week, +33.9% in three months.

Hedging demand finally arrived and it is spot-driven, not tail-driven: VIX +18.7% to 22.91, VIX3M +11.6%, VIX/VIX3M at 0.995, while SKEW is -13.2% on the month at z=-2.0 (acc -2.63). Forced selling, not insurance.

Asia's semiconductor complex is in day-three liquidation and the US proxies have not marked it: TAIEX -6.9% after -6.0%, KOSPI -4.7% (23.4% below its 200-day), Nikkei -3.4%; SMH -13.8% 1m, NVDA -26.4% at the 0th percentile.

Brazil is the accelerating accident: USDBRL +2.1% to 5.7838, +13.5% on the month at z=3.81 with acceleration 2.80, Bovespa z=-3.39, EWZ -24.4% on the month. The dollar is at the 100th percentile with EURUSD at the 0th.

The industrial-metal message keeps worsening: copper -8.3% on the month, COPX -14.3%, FCX -14.7%, XME -6.1%, silver -17.1% and 30.8% below its 200-day, gold/silver at the 100th percentile. Demand, not the monetary bid, is what is breaking.

trades.name: Taiwan/Korea catch-down
trades.line: Short EWT + EWY: US proxies still owe two days of Asia losses
trades.expr: Short EWT 1.0, short EWY 0.5; or buy Dec EWT puts ~5% OTM if borrow is tight.
trades.thesis: The semiconductor de-rating is being liquidated where the supply chain actually sits. Taiwan and Korea local indices have fallen two consecutive sessions on heavy acceleration, but the US-listed ETFs were last marked before the second leg and still show only -12.2% and -10.7% on the month.
trades.trigger: TWII -6.9% today after -6.0% yesterday (z=-2.59, acceleration -1.93); KOSPI -4.7% and 23.4% below its 200-day; SMH/SPY at z=-2.02; NVDA at the 0th percentile of its year.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY reclaims its 200-day or EWT closes +4% from entry with VIX back below 19 — that says the gap already closed and dip-buyers won.
trades.target: 8-10% on the basket as EWT/EWY converge to local index prints.

trades.name: Cash-flow-now vs discount-rate
trades.line: Long XLV / short SMH: 2.91% real yields pick the winner
trades.thesis: With the 10-year real yield at 2.91% and 29.5% above its 200-day, the market is discounting terminal-value stories and paying for current earnings. Health care is the only sector with both near-52-week-high relative strength and positive acceleration; semis are the funding leg of every de-grossing.
trades.trigger: XLV +8.6% 1m, +10.8% relative strength, 98th percentile, z=1.94; SMH -13.8% 1m, rolling over, relative strength -12.1%; LLY +19.6% on the month; growth/value z=-2.48.
trades.stop: Breakevens turn up and real 10-year drops back below 2.70%, or SMH/SPY closes two days above its 200-day. A dovish Fed pivot kills this pair.

trades.name: Short long-end duration
trades.line: Short TLT: 30y 5.47%, MOVE 101, and no bid for term premium
trades.expr: Short TLT outright (or buy Jan TLT puts ~4% OTM); size half of a normal rates clip given MOVE at 101.
trades.thesis: Equity weakness is not producing a duration bid. Yields rose across the curve on a -1.9% S&P day, which is the signature of supply and term premium, not growth fear. With bond vol at 101 and the 2-year +37bp in a week, the long end has no sponsor.
trades.trigger: 10y 5.15% (+5bp), 30y 5.47% (+4bp), real 10y +5bp — all higher while SPX fell 1.9%; MOVE +17.8% on the week; TLT trend down at the 24th percentile of its year.
trades.stop: TLT +4% from entry, which would mean the equity drawdown has finally flipped into a flight-to-quality / growth-scare regime and the trade thesis is void.

trades.name: Long USD/BRL
trades.line: Long USDBRL: z=3.81 and accelerating for a second day
trades.expr: Long USDBRL spot/forward; alternatively short EWZ as the equity expression.
trades.thesis: This is the most extreme and most accelerating dislocation on the board, and unlike the Asia equity unwind it has no offsetting local bid. A 100th-percentile dollar plus collapsing commodity terms of trade is the exact cocktail that keeps a funding-stress move running past the point of 'overbought'.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +2.1% to 5.7838, +13.5% on the month, z=3.81 with acceleration 2.80; Bovespa z=-3.39, EWZ -24.4% 1m; DXY at the 100th percentile; copper -8.3% and oil -16.1% on the month.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.55 (-3%) or two consecutive down days with EWZ up more than 3% — that signals local policy intervention has worked.

trades.name: Fade the E&P bid
trades.line: Short XOP: crude -16% on the month, E&Ps +6.3% on the week
trades.expr: Short XOP; keep it small, it is a divergence trade not a trend trade.
trades.thesis: Energy equities rallied hard into a crude market that is breaking. E&P cash flows are price-takers; a 16% monthly decline in WTI and a 23% decline in gasoline cracks does not coexist with XOP at the 76th percentile of its year for long.
trades.trigger: WTI -3.9% today to 85.09 (z=-1.64, acc -0.96), Brent -4.3%, gasoline -5.0% and -23.0% on the month; yet XOP +6.3% on the week and XLE +5.4%, with XOP relative strength turning up.
trades.stop: WTI closes back above 90 or Brent reclaims its 200-day — any supply headline reverses this immediately.

trades.name: Pump-price dividend vs mega-cap tech
trades.line: Long XRT / short QQQ into the holiday consumer
trades.thesis: The single cleanest transmission of the energy collapse is consumer discretionary spending power, and the labour market is still funding it. Meanwhile QQQ carries all the real-rate duration risk. This pair monetises the dispersion without taking a net market view.
trades.trigger: Gasoline -23.0% on the month at z=-2.10; XRT/SPY z=1.95 with acceleration 1.57; XLY +7.6% 1m and turning up; claims 200k and continuing claims at the 1st percentile; QQQ -6.7% 1m, rolling over, QQQ/SPY z=-1.92.
trades.stop: -5% on the spread, or continuing claims breaking above 1.75m — a cracking labour market invalidates the consumer leg faster than cheap gas helps it.
